attempts.title: Attempt 1: balance → step → walk → walk fast
attempts.note: Stage rewards as first designed (see the stage table).

spec.name: Balance
terms: for staying up the whole episode
average |hull angle| in radians: keep the body level
effort = 0.028 × |motor command| per joint per step, summed
spec.episode: 500 steps (10 s), no early stop: standing still is allowed
spec.pass: 0 falls on 20 held-out tracks and average |tilt| < 0.15 rad
spec.expect: Stands upright on any track, body level, using little motor effort. Maximum score ≈ 100.
spec.risk: Locks into a stiff split stance (one foot forward). Harmless here, since stage 2 has to break it anyway.

stages.name: Step
stages.desc: alternating front-foot changes, even in place, 600 steps

spec.name: Step
spec.reward: 100 × survival − 100 × fell + 3 × front-foot changes (max 40) + alternating touchdowns (max 60) − 30 × |average foot offset| − 0.5 × effort
terms: the foot in front changes (lower legs pass each other by > 0.15), up to 40 changes = 120
a foot touches down after the OTHER foot did (left, right, left…), up to 60
average distance foot 1 is ahead of foot 2: keeps the feet centred, no permanent lead
spec.episode: 600 steps (12 s), no early stop: stepping in place is fine, moving forward is neither paid nor punished
spec.pass: ≤ 1 fall in 20, ≥ 12 front-foot changes per episode, |average offset| < 0.5
spec.expect: Marches in place or creeps forward, legs swinging past each other in turn, left-right-left touchdowns, without falling. Maximum ≈ 100 + 120 + 60 = 280.
spec.risk: Shuffles the feet back and forth while sliding them, so the front-foot changes count without real steps. The alternating-touchdown term is there to require lifting.

stages.name: Walk
stages.desc: distance with the gait tax, full episodes

spec.name: Walk
spec.reward: environment reward (fall costs 20 instead of 100) − (40 × lopsided + 20 × |average offset|) × share of the course covered
terms: the environment's motor cost, per unit per step
for a fall (the real game charges 100; training uses 20 so trying steps isn't too costly)
lopsided = |2 × (share of leading time foot 2 leads) − 1|: 0 if the feet take turns, 1 if one always leads
how far one foot sits ahead on average
the gait tax grows with distance: standing pays nothing, a full-length skip pays ≈ 77
spec.episode: full 1600 steps; early stop if the body moves < 1 unit in 150 steps
spec.expect: Turns the march into forward walking: alternating steps that carry the body most of the way along the course.
spec.risk: Drifts back to the skip (one leg as a prop), or stumbles forward and falls, as v5-fresh did.

stages.name: Walk fast
stages.desc: the real reward plus the gait tax

spec.name: Walk fast
spec.reward: the real environment reward (fall −100) − (40 × lopsided + 20 × |average offset|) × share of the course covered
terms: a fall, as in the real game
as in stage 3, so the form stays while it speeds up
spec.episode: full 1600 steps, early stop on stall
spec.pass: no stage test: runs until it plateaus or 6 h; then the goal check below
spec.expect: The same alternating walk, faster and cheaper: reaches the finish with less effort and few falls, raw score ≥ 250.
spec.risk: Speed returns the skip (cheaper per unit) if the tax is too small; or more falls as it speeds up.

attempts.title: Attempt 2: balance with feet together → real steps → walk → walk fast
attempts.note: Attempt 1's balance champion stood with its feet 2.9 units apart, foot 2 always in front (the skipper's stance). Its step stage then learned to TAP its feet alternately in that split stance: ~70 alternating touchdowns, 0 front-foot changes, σ collapsed to 0.013. Attempt 2 balances with the feet together, and only counts a touchdown as a step when the foot coming down is the front foot. Stages 3 and 4 are unchanged.

spec.name: Balance (feet together)
spec.reward: 100 × (steps survived ÷ 500) − 100 × fell − 50 × average |body tilt| − 0.5 × effort − 30 × |average foot offset|
terms: for staying up the whole episode
average |hull angle| in radians: keep the body level
effort = 0.028 × |motor command| per joint per step, summed
how far one foot stands ahead of the other on average: a centred stance, not the skipper's split stance
spec.episode: 500 steps (10 s), no early stop: standing still is allowed
spec.pass: 0 falls on 20 held-out tracks, average |tilt| < 0.15 rad, |average offset| < 0.4
spec.expect: Stands upright and level with the feet close together, so either leg can take the first step. Maximum ≈ 100.
spec.risk: Can't find a stable narrow stance (the base is short), or keeps a small split anyway; the offset term and the pass test guard against that.

spec.name: Step (real steps only)

terms: the lower legs pass each other (by > 0.15), up to 40 = 120
a foot touches down while it is the FRONT foot, and it's the other leg from the last counted one: a real step. Tapping in a split stance only ever counts one leg. Up to 40 = 80
spec.episode: 600 steps (12 s), no early stop: stepping in place is fine, moving forward is neither paid nor punished
spec.pass: ≤ 1 fall in 20, ≥ 12 front-foot changes and ≥ 10 front-foot touchdowns per episode, |offset| < 0.5, lopsided ≤ 0.4
spec.expect: Steps in place or creeps forward with real steps: the swinging foot lands in front, legs taking turns. Maximum ≈ 100 + 120 + 80 = 300; the attempt-1 tapper scores 47 here.
spec.risk: Some other way to swap feet without lifting them (sliding), or stepping so hard that it falls.

journal.title: Attempt 1 found a shortcut: tapping in a split stance. Attempt 2 started.
journal.text: Stage 1 of attempt 1 passed, but its champion balances with its feet 2.9 units apart, foot 2 always in front: the skipper's stance. Stage 2 then learned to tap its feet alternately in that stance: about 70 alternating touchdowns per episode and zero front-foot changes, so the feet never pass each other, and the search has stopped exploring (σ 0.013). Attempt 2 fixes both: stage 1 now also pays for keeping the feet together, and stage 2 only counts a touchdown as a step when the foot coming down is the front foot and the legs alternate. Under the new step reward the tapper drops from 105 to 47 points while a real stepper can earn about 300. Attempt 1 keeps running as the baseline.

journal.title: v7-alt stopped; the curriculum gets the whole machine
journal.text: v7-alt (warm start from the alternating stumbler, with the per-distance gait tax) kept alternating, with foot 2 leading about 52% of the time and roughly 15 front-foot changes per episode, but after 177 generations every training episode still ended in a fall around x = 14. It is kept below as a comparison but no longer trains, so the curriculum runs alone on the four cores. The local dashboard on port 8771 now follows whichever curriculum stage is active.

journal.title: Curriculum started
journal.text: Every earlier attempt at proper walking had to find balance, alternating steps and forward progress at once, and settled for a shortcut each time: skipping with one leg as a prop (v3, v4, v5-warm), stumbling forward with alternating steps and falling (v5-fresh), or standing still (v6). The curriculum gives each skill its own training reward: 1 balance, 2 step (alternating feet, even in place), 3 walk, 4 walk fast. Each stage starts from the previous stage's champion. Attempt 1 started Wednesday 08:15. Running alongside for comparison: v7-alt, which starts from the alternating stumbler and has to learn balance while walking.
